title: Tool Chain Data Exfiltration (read then send)
summary: Two individually low-risk tool calls combine into exfiltration of credentials. In the lab the outbound step is logged, not sent.

LC.rationale: Attacker-supplied tool arguments (file path, exfil URL) reach privileged tool-invocation paths (read_file, fetch_url) over unauthenticated JSON-RPC with no mediation, and PluginBot accepts unverified tool registrations.

CP.rationale: The path is stateless: MCP tools/call requests do their work in one request; the profile shows no cross-session memory except MemoryBot, which is not on this path.

AP.rationale: Both steps (read_file then fetch_url) execute inside ToolBot's own handler under the same principal; no other agent, tenant, or policy domain is reached in the default implementation.

RH.rationale: No model, evaluator, verifier, or reward channel exists on this path in the default configuration (no API key, no model invoked), so there is no proxy objective for the agent to hack.

ES.rationale: PluginBot registers tools at runtime with no signature or source check, and ToolBot's fetch_url takes an arbitrary external URL (logged), so the extension surface is dynamic and unconstrained.

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. The lab models this challenge as attacker-driven tool chaining over MCP; the challenge text describes the attacker registering and calling the two tools, with the agent never choosing or ordering the actions itself.
